page.layout: One page of text, one column. Running head at the top left, page number at the top right. A centred heading (EXERC. XXVI.) and a centred two-line title (the second line italic), then the running text with an initial P. No marginal notes, no footnotes. Gathering signature and catchword at the foot.

main_text.p: item & melancholici, quòd minus habent humoris aere pestifero tardius afficiuntur, & praesertim melancholici, quorum corpora duriora sunt, ac ficciora. Citius igitur bi-liosos pestis adoritur, quòd calidiores sint. Eos quoq; silentio non praetereo, qui Dei optimi nutu, & mirabili modo ab hoc vitae periculo liberantur. Non desunt etiam ad praecautione alexiteria, & aduersus ipsam pestem amuleta: Sed omnium optimum conferuans est ab hac lue celeris fuga, & hinc procul, ac etiam illuc tardus reditus.

Unde hoc natum est proverbium: Abi cito, & longè, & tardè redi. Quod fane duntaxat privatis suadeo, non autè publico fungentibus officio, qui salutem universi vitae suae quantumuis charae anteponere debent.

page.notes: The page number 119 is printed at the top right; its 9 is a turned, somewhat worn form, read here as 9. The initial P of the last paragraph is a large woodcut-style letter, joined to "Estem" as "PEstem". The accent on "quòd" and "autè" and "venenatâ" appears as printed; the accent over "quòd" is faint, so the reading "quòd" is slightly uncertain. "ę" in "exitiosę" and "charae" follows the print. The running head is set in small capitals and is read as CAUSAS, PROGYMNASMATA. Line-end hyphens "bi-", "ca-", "PROFLI-" and "pharmaco-" are printed hyphens and are kept.
